```{r}
data2024 = read_csv("clean_data/nov24pub_clean.csv")
data2022 = read_csv("clean_data/nov22pub_clean.csv")
data2020 = read_csv("clean_data/nov20pub_clean.csv")
data2018 = read_csv("clean_data/nov18pub_clean.csv")
data2016 = read_csv("clean_data/nov16pub_clean.csv")
data2014 = read_csv("clean_data/nov14pub_clean.csv")
data2012 = read_csv("clean_data/nov12pub_clean.csv")
data2010 = read_csv("clean_data/nov10pub_clean.csv")

data = bind_rows(data2024, data2022, data2020, data2020, data2018, data2016, data2014, data2012, data2010)
data
```
```{r}
y = as.factor(data$PES1)
X <- data[, !names(data) %in% c("PES1", "PES2")]

set.seed(42)
sample_idx <- sample(nrow(X), 10000)  # 10k rows is plenty for variable selection
X <- X[sample_idx, ]
y <- y[sample_idx]

# These are CPS admin columns, not predictors
drop_cols <- c("HRHHID", "HRMONTH", "HRYEAR4", "HURESPLI", "HUFINAL", "FILLER")
X <- X[, !names(X) %in% drop_cols]

pes_cols <- grep("^PES", names(X), value = TRUE)
X <- X[, !names(X) %in% pes_cols]

weight_cols <- grep("^PW|^HW", names(X), value = TRUE)
X <- X[, !names(X) %in% weight_cols]
X <- X[, !names(X) %in% c("HRHHID2")]

cat("Working with:", nrow(X), "rows,", ncol(X), "cols\n")

# Remove columns that are constant OR all NA
zero_var <- apply(X, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
bad_cols <- is.na(zero_var) | zero_var == 0
cat("Removing", sum(bad_cols), "zero-variance or all-NA columns the bad columns are: ", bad_cols,"\n")
X <- X[, !bad_cols]

# Also good practice: remove near-zero variance
low_var <- apply(X, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-10
X <- X[, !low_var]

X <- as.data.frame(lapply(X, function(col) {
  col[is.na(col)] <- -1  # -1 = "not asked / not applicable"
  col
}))
```
```{r}
# ── 1. Build modules (same as before) ──────────────────────────────────────
cor_mat <- cor(X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Check for any NaN left
any(is.nan(cor_mat))  # should be FALSE

# If still TRUE, find and drop the offending columns
bad_cols <- apply(cor_mat, 2, function(x) any(is.nan(x)))
cat("Dropping", sum(bad_cols), "columns with NaN correlations\n")
X <- X[, !bad_cols]

# Recompute and cluster
cor_mat <- cor(X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Find which columns produce NaN correlations
nan_cols <- apply(cor_mat, 2, function(x) any(is.nan(x)))
cat("Columns with NaN correlations:", sum(nan_cols), "\n")
cat(names(nan_cols[nan_cols]), "\n")  # see which ones

# Drop them
X <- X[, !nan_cols]

# Recompute
# Keep only columns that have no NaN in their entire correlation row/col
cor_mat <- cor(X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
keep <- apply(cor_mat, 2, function(x) all(!is.nan(x)) && all(!is.na(x)))
X <- X[, keep]

cor_mat <- cor(X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
dist_mat <- as.dist(1 - abs(cor_mat))
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "average")
module_membership <- cutree(hc, k = 5)

# Confirm it exists
table(module_membership)

# Plot the dendrogram to see where natural breaks are
plot(hc, labels = FALSE, hang = -1)
abline(h = 0.5, col = "red")  # visualize where h cuts
```
```{r}
module_membership <- cutree(hc, h = 0.3)
cat("Number of modules:", length(unique(module_membership)), "\n")
table(module_membership)
```

```{r}
# ── 2. Screen within each module ───────────────────────────────────────────
keep_fraction <- 0.25  # keep top 25% of vars from each module
survivors <- c()

for (mod in unique(module_membership)) {
  mod_vars <- names(module_membership[module_membership == mod])
  
  # need at least 2 vars to run a forest
  if (length(mod_vars) < 2) {
    survivors <- c(survivors, mod_vars)
    next
  }
  
  X_mod <- X[, mod_vars, drop = FALSE]
  
  rf_mod <- randomForest(
    x = X_mod,
    y = y,
    ntree = 500,
    importance = TRUE
  )
  
  imp <- importance(rf_mod, type = 1)  # mean decrease accuracy
  imp_sorted <- sort(imp[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
  
  n_keep <- max(1, ceiling(length(mod_vars) * keep_fraction))
  survivors <- c(survivors, names(imp_sorted)[1:n_keep])
}

cat("Survivors after screening:", length(survivors), "\n")

# ── 3. Final forest on survivors ───────────────────────────────────────────
X_survivors <- X[, survivors, drop = FALSE]

set.seed(42)
rf_final <- randomForest(
  x = X_survivors,
  y = y,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)

# ── 4. Rank final variable importance ──────────────────────────────────────
final_imp <- importance(rf_final, type = 1)
final_imp_sorted <- sort(final_imp[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
top_vars <- names(final_imp_sorted)[1:25]  # top 25

print(final_imp_sorted[1:25])

```
```{r}
# ── 5. Plot ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
library(ggplot2)

imp_df <- data.frame(
  variable   = names(final_imp_sorted[1:25]),
  importance = final_imp_sorted[1:25]
)

ggplot(imp_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, importance), y = importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Fuzzy Forest Variable Importance",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean Decrease Accuracy") +
  theme_minimal()
```
